messages:
olivia: Quick sync — saw a support ticket where a customer treated a 200+\"degraded_route\" body as success and didn't surface the fallback to users. We should align: HTTP status vs in-body signal, console badge copy, and telemetry tags. TL;DR: proposal below, want opinions + rollout plan.

mike: +1 we keep mixing semantics. historically we've used 200 for soft-fallbacks to avoid breaking clients, but that hides failures from naive callers.

priya: Agree. The core tension: preservation of backwards compatibility for many SDKs vs making errors observable in logs and SLOs.

olivia: Proposal A (conservative): keep 200 for soft degradations but add a top-level `x-route-status` header and `route_status` field in body. Console shows yellow badge "degraded" and telemetry emits `route.status=degraded`. SDKs map to `response.routeStatus`.

olivia: Example payload (conservative):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-route-status: degraded
{
  "id":"resp_abc",
  "route_status":"degraded",
  "fallback_model":"gpt-compat-1",
  "output":"..."
}
```

mike: Proposal B (strict): return 503 for routed degradations that materially change semantics (e.g., shorter context, non-deterministic model). Pros: SLOs/alerts immediately fire. Cons: potentially breaks integrations expecting a 200.

priya: If we do B we need a phased rollout + feature flag per tenant. Also need clear console copy and runbooks for customers.

taylor: From console/UX POV, the text matters more than numeric status. If we stick with 200 we must make the yellow badge copy explicit: "Degraded: using fallback model, behavior may differ. See runbook." Short and actionable.

olivia: Also telemetry naming: current tag is `route.degraded` (boolean). Suggest normalize to `route.status` with values [ok,degraded,fallback,failed]. That lets dashboards pivot easily. Thoughts?

mike: I like `route.status` enum. Also emit `route.fallback_model` and `route.reason_code` (e.g., `quota_throttled`, `node_unavailable`, `safety_triggered`).

priya: +1. We should also emit `client_visible=true/false` to indicate whether we consider this user-visible degradation. That helps downstream alerting.

taylor: Console badge copy proposals: short: "Degraded — fallback model in use." hover/click: "Requests are routed to a fallback model to preserve availability. Expect different output quality and latency. Learn how to opt into Dedicated capacity or pin model versions."

mike: SDK surface: add `response.signal.route_status` and `response.signal.reason_code`. Default SDK behavior: log a warning once per request if status != ok. Provide opt-out.

olivia: Rollout plan idea:
1) Add header + body fields + telemetry (no change to status codes) behind a global flag — roll to hosted first.
2) Update Console: new badge + link to runbook.
3) Update SDKs to surface signals and warn.
4) After 4 weeks of telemetry indicating <0.1% breakage on a canary cohort, start opt-in beta for 5xx on degradations for a subset of tenants.

priya: Need to define metric for "breakage". Suggest: increase in client error events that correlate with downstream ingestion failures > X p95. We can instrument a synthetic signal.

mike: Also ensure retrofit of existing dashboards to use `route.status` so customers can alert. I'll file a PR to the telemetry schema.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: telemetry-schema/pr -> staging on 1769999500 by @mike.

olivia: Action items: @mike open telemetry PR; @priya add feature flag and runbook skeleton; @taylor draft badge copy and link text; I'll prepare comms and support FAQ.

mike: I'll start the PR now. putting a short TODO in it for the `reason_code` enums.

priya: I'll prototype feature flag gate and a per-tenant opt-in for strict 5xx routing.

taylor: I'll drop three variants of the badge copy into the console mock channel for quick review.

olivia: Thanks all — will follow up with a short RFC doc. If nobody objects in 24h we go with Proposal A rollout plan. :thumbsup:
